{{Quote|There is no passion&hellip;there is solely obsession.<br />There is no knowledge. There is solely conviction.<br />There is no purpose. There is solely will.<br />There is nothing&hellip;<br />Only me.|The creed of Ruin|<ref name="EOTJ">{{DoD|Echoes of the Jedi}}</ref>}}
'''Darth Ruin''', formerly known as '''Phanius''', was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] who reigned as a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] at the beginning of the [[Draggulch Period]] in around [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]]. Previously an esteemed [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], Phanius gained notoriety within the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] due to his prominently self-centered philosophy—the idea that his very will superseded everything in existence. At odds with the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi tenets]], Phanius eventually abandoned the Order in pursuit of his individualistic ideology, steering him towards the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and leading him on an alternate path—the way of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].

Intent on reviving the Sith into a new [[Sith Empire (disambiguation)|empire]], Phanius rallied various surviving [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith clans]] under his banner. The former Jedi Master then declared himself a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] under the new identity of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Ruin, simultaneously converting fifty additional [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in the [[Fourth Great Schism]]. Finalizing the [[New Sith|Sith resurgence]], [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Ruin gave rise to a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]]-scale conflict—the [[New Sith Wars]]—against the Jedi Order and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

The reign of Darth Ruin met an untimely end due to the Dark Lord's own ruthless egomania, evoking the wrath of his Sith disciples and resulting in his [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]]. In spite of Ruin's [[Death/Legends|death]], his machinations left behind an enduringly [[Blood/Legends|bloody]] legacy; the Sith crusades—while frequently plagued by disagreement and backstabbing—continued for a [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]] in his absence, bringing [[Galactic Republic/Legends|galactic civilization]] to the [[Republic Dark Age|brink of collapse]].

==Biography==
===Rise of the New Sith===
{{Quote|A mysterious figure who may have been an Umbaran, Darth Ruin revived the Sith Order and seduced a number of Jedi to his cause. A war with the Jedi Order inevitably followed, but the Sith soon turned the war upon themselves. Ruin was destroyed by his own disciples, who ushered in a millennium-long period of betrayal and darkness amongst the Sith.|Bodo Baas's writings|<ref name="JVS" />}}
[[File:Darth_Ruin-BoS.jpg|thumb|left|160px|Darth Ruin, Dark Lord of the Sith]]
A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]],<ref name="END" /> Phanius was a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] of the peacekeeping [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] who lived near the advent of the [[Draggulch Period]], an era beginning in [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]] during the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" /> Up to this point, Phanius had attained a polarizing reputation in his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] career. While highly regarded for his intellect and charisma, the Jedi Master unsettled many of his peers<ref name="END" />—even facing condemnation from the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]<ref name="TPM">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>—by exhibiting solipsistic traits; the Umbaran had begun to perceive his own mind and, by extension, himself, as the only thing to truly exist.<ref name="END" /> Upon realizing the Order's refusal to accept his stance,<ref name="TPM" /> Phanius chose to abandon the ways of the Jedi, driven to uncover alternate teachings that would allow him to fully embrace his individualistic ideology.<ref name="END" /> Having renounced his place among the Jedi, he became formally recognized as one of "[[Lost Twenty/Legends|The Lost]]"—Jedi Masters who voluntarily left the Order over ideological differences.<ref name="JVS" />

At some stage in his quest for knowledge,<ref name="END" /> Phanius managed to obtain a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]]—a crystalline data storage device—from a [[Jedi temple/Legends|Jedi temple]]. The device in question contained teachings of the [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]]-old [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]], a cult that adhered to the ways of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="DSSB">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> By around this point, Phanius himself had [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen]] under the dark side's corruptive power, though his former Jedi allies remained completely oblivious to his conversion at the time.<ref name="JVS" /> Armed with his new-found knowledge of the dark side,<ref name="DSSB" /> the former Jedi Master set out to recruit more disciples to the ways of the Sith,<ref name="END" /> vowing revenge against the Jedi Order for dismissing his beliefs.<ref name="TPM" />

In an effort to revive the Sith Order, Phanius sought out a number of [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith clans]] that had survived throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="END" /> disproving the common belief that the dark side cult had been destroyed for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] up to this time.<ref name="JVS" /> Working outside of the Jedi Order's notice, he managed to infiltrate and unite these clans,<ref name="END" /> paving the way for what would ultimately become a new [[Empire (disambiguation)|empire]] of the [[Sith Empire (disambiguation)|Sith]].<ref name="TEA" /> In the process, Phanius relinquished his former identity—determined to break his mental barriers in pursuit of egocentric self-interest—and declared himself a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] under the new moniker of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Ruin. With his new title,<ref name="END" /> the Dark Lord convinced fifty additional Jedi to leave the Order and rally behind his cause, resulting in the<ref name="TEA" /> [[Fourth Great Schism]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

The culmination of Darth Ruin's machinations gave rise to the [[New Sith]],<ref name="END" /> a resurgent Sith faction that engaged the Jedi Order and the Republic in a [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict called the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="TEA" /> By the time of his reign over the Sith, Darth Ruin had enlisted a squire by the name of [[Eradicus]].<ref name="BOS" /> The Dark Lord held his disciples in low regard, viewing them literally as "nothing" in the grand scheme of his individualistic obsession. This attitude led Ruin to [[Death/Legends|sacrifice]] many of his Sith followers seemingly on a whim, provoking their ire and eventually driving them to conspire against him.<ref name="END" /> Despite the murderous intent of his disgruntled underlings, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Ruin never even considered the possibility that they would bring about his demise.<ref name="JVS" /> This single-minded confidence facilitated a premature end to the reign of the new Dark Lord, resulting in his [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]].<ref name="END" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Darth Ruin, who left the Jedi Order to pursue his monomaniacal philosophy of self-interest and gave rise to the thousand-year war that concluded at Ruusan, and who was among the last to hold the Darth title—until I took it up again.|Darth Bane's writings|<ref name="BOS" />}}
[[File:NewSithWars.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Ruin initiated the New Sith Wars, a thousand-year conflict that brought galactic civilization to the brink of collapse.]]
The actions of the late Darth Ruin brought about a new age of expansion and reclamation for the Sith. Even in his absence, the New Sith Wars persisted for a thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. During this time, a number of Dark Lords rose to leadership in various destructive campaigns against the Jedi and the Republic, pushing the latter to the brink of collapse. Among these leading figures was [[Darth Rivan]],<ref name="TEA" /> a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] who at one point owned a [[Book/Legends|scripture]] containing a text passage in the [[Sith (language)|Sith language]]—titled the "creed of ruin"—reminiscent of Ruin's solipsistic philosophy.<ref name="EOTJ" /> Despite a string of crushing victories achieved by Ruin's successors,<ref name="TEA" /> the treachery that originally led to his death continued to plague the Sith ranks, with many subsequent Dark Lords falling to the same fate.<ref name="BOS" />

At some point during the [[Republic Dark Age]] that began in [[1100 BBY/Legends|1100 BBY]], the Sith finally turned against one another in a [[Blood/Legends|bloody]] period of [[Sith civil war|civil war]], fracturing the empire that Ruin had founded. The Sith remnants were later reorganized into the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], only to meet their ultimate demise at the [[Ruusan campaign|conclusion]] of the New Sith Wars in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> A lone Brotherhood survivor—[[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]]<ref name="BOS" />—went on to establish a [[Rule of Two/Legends|new Sith doctrine]] to overcome the pitfalls that destroyed Ruin and his successors,<ref name="END" /> of which Bane discussed in a historical compilation called the ''[[Book of Sith]]''.<ref name="BOS" /> The Jedi Order expressed a grim view of Ruin's legacy in a guidebook titled [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|''The Jedi Path'']], stating that his revival of the Sith nearly led to the end of galactic civilization.<ref name="TJP" />

In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], an [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force|encyclopedic compendium]] about [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]—compiled by [[Jedi historian]] [[Tionne Solusar]]—briefly explored details regarding Ruin's former life as a Jedi Master, as well as his motivations for leaving the Order and establishing the New Sith.<ref name="JVS" />

==Personality and traits==
A pale<ref name="END" /> blue-skinned<ref name="BOS" /> member of the Umbaran [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="END" /> Master Phanius stood among the most charismatic and talented Jedi of his time.<ref name="JVS" /> In spite of this, the Jedi Master stirred controversy with his intellectual pursuits, particularly his growing fascination with the philosophy of solipsism.<ref name="END" /> An ambitious,<ref name="TPM" /> abstract thinker, Phanius believed that his own perceptions superseded all things in existence, meaning that—from his point of view—he was essentially the ''only'' thing to exist. This self-centered mindset led Phanius to resent the Jedi Order for not accepting his vision;<ref name="END" /><ref name="TPM" /> he came to view the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi teachings]] as a hindrance, one that would prevent the Umbaran from fully realizing that he was, in fact, "everything". Determined to obliterate these inhibitions, Phanius fell to the dark side and pursued the alternate path of the Sith, assuming the identity of Darth Ruin as a Dark Lord. Throughout his campaign to revive the Sith, Ruin grew increasingly consumed by his individualistic obsession, developing a sense of utter detachment from his Sith disciples.<ref name="END" /> Many of Ruin's followers fell victim to his ruthless impulses, making him a widely detested leader and, ultimately, a target for assassination. Nonetheless, the Dark Lord maintained an unyielding confidence in his monomaniacal pursuit,<ref name="JVS" /><ref name="BOS" /> leaving him completely blind to the treachery that would bring about his death.<ref name="JVS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Ruin is the definition of pure evil, as I conceive of him and it. I'd say he is in the Darth Traya mold, only Ruin broke the mold and then murdered the mold-maker.|[[Abel G. Peña]]|<ref name="Pena quote">{{WebCite|url=http://www.thesithorder.com/index.php?name=PNphpBB2&file=viewtopic&p=55945|text=Interview with Abel G. Peña|date=2009-01-19|archivedate=20090709015637}}</ref>}}
Darth Ruin was first mentioned as an unidentified [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]-turned-[[Sith/Legends|Sith]] in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], written by [[Terry Brooks]] and published in [[1999]]. The book cites Ruin as having founded the Sith as a whole "almost two thousand years ago,"<ref name="TPM" /> contradicting the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] comics.<ref name="TOTJ">[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'' comic series]]</ref> In [[2000]], this inconsistency was explained in [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']], establishing the still-unidentified Ruin as the creator of a successor faction—the [[New Sith]].<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> The character was officially named Darth Ruin by author [[Abel G. Peña]] in ''[[Vader: The Ultimate Guide]]'', a limited edition magazine released in [[2005]].<ref name="Vader">''[[Vader: The Ultimate Guide]]''</ref> To this end, Peña saw the name Ruin—derived from the Latin word "ruīna", meaning "fall"—as a fitting representation of the character's fall to the dark side, as well as the destructive chaos following his demise. Several other Darth titles were considered, such as Reaper, Fatalis, Necro, Mortalis, Eradicus, Execute and Solopsis. While creating Ruin's backstory, Peña envisioned him as an intelligent, wise and evil individual in the same vein as [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] from the [[Prequel trilogy|''Star Wars'' prequel films]],<ref name="Abel-Ruin">{{Blog|abelgpena|58|Ruining Lives, Just Ruining Lives: or, A Darth By Any Other Name, Part 1}}</ref> as well as [[Kreia|Darth Traya]] from the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''.<ref name="Pena quote" /> In [[2006]], Peña further expanded Ruin's history in an article titled ''[[Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties]]'', confirming his species as an [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] and former identity as a Jedi Master named Phanius.<ref name="END" />
